name: Small estate agency trust-account audit and FICA pack (PPRA audit file, FIC registration, RMCP, RCR)
buyer: Principals of small and one-person estate agencies, which also covers property practitioners without a trust-account exemption
trigger: Property Practitioners Act 22 of 2019: trust account audit within 6 months of year-end, filed by the IRBA-registered auditor on the MyPPRA Auditors Portal; PPRA refused extensions (Feb 2025 year-end cut-off was 31 Aug 2025). FIC Act: registration, RMCP, compliance officer, annual Risk and Compliance Return (30 Jun 2026) and RMCP submission directive. The Fidelity Fund Certificate renewal can be blocked by late audits.
existing: REBOSA free RMCP template, a CDH pro forma template, and the Moonstone FICA Toolkit (a document toolkit, not workflow software). The competitor search found no workflow software for small agencies. Late-fee amounts were from a secondary source and are unverified.
unchecked: Whether MyPPRA or estate-agency back-office software already prompts audit prep; FIC goAML reporting steps for agents; the real size of the small-agency segment after PPRA exemptions; Fidelity Fund Certificate renewal timing.

first_check.duty: Confirmed. Property Practitioners Act 22 of 2019: practitioners with trust accounts need a yearly trust-account audit, submitted by an IRBA-registered auditor on the MyPPRA Auditors Portal within 6 months of year-end (31 Aug for a Feb year-end). The PPRA says it grants no extensions. Late-penalty figures differ between sources (R20/day for 3 months vs a R25,000 fine) and come from secondary sources, so they are unverified. FIC Act: estate agents are accountable institutions and must register on goAML, keep an RMCP and file the RCR. Final Directive 12 (Gazette 55337, 4 Sep 2026) requires an RMCP upload to goAML every year, with estate agents (item 3) due 31 Oct, moved from 30 Sep in the draft (Moonstone). Directive 10 asks for geographic particulars by 31 Oct 2026. Sanctions: up to R50m for legal persons; Capital Point Properties got a R266,000 penalty that the Appeal Board upheld in Aug 2024. The FFC can be delayed if FIC compliance or the audit is outstanding (propertyprofessional.co.za, May 2026).
first_check.market: Not verified. I found no PPRA or FIC count of registered agencies, FFC holders or goAML-registered estate agents. The PPRA 2025/26 APP PDF could not be read, and searches for the annual report returned no figures. Directive 6 RCR compliance among estate agents was reported at about 50%, which suggests many laggards. The segment is likely several thousand firms, but that is an estimate and needs checking.
first_check.competitor: I found no integrated workflow tool for small agencies that combines audit prep, RMCP, RCR and the Directive 12 upload. Partial competitors: the Moonstone FICA Toolkit (a document toolkit at R4,995 excl VAT plus hourly implementation help; it doesn't cover the RCR or records); the REBOSA free RMCP template (2019, may be out of date); The Virtual Agent's FICA & Fraud module (client KYC with a Home Affairs check, not RMCP or reporting); KYC Africa (nCino), which publishes an AML toolkit for estate agents; PropData, which writes about agency FICA practices; and IEASA webinars and consultants (e.g. MJK Inc FICA service for estate agents). Trust-accounting and rental software (e.g. PayProp) probably covers the ledger side but was not checked. Whether MyPPRA prompts audit prep: not reached.
first_check.reason: The duties are real and recur. A PPRA trust-account audit is due within 6 months of year-end, filed by an IRBA auditor on MyPPRA, with no extensions. Final FIC Directive 12 (Gazette 4 Sep 2026) adds a yearly RMCP upload to goAML, due 31 Oct for estate agents, on top of the RCR. The FFC can be withheld. I found no integrated workflow software, only templates (REBOSA, Moonstone's R4,995 toolkit) and KYC tools (TVA, KYC Africa). Limits: the audit must be done by an auditor, so software can only help prepare for it. Small agencies spend little and lean on auditors and franchise groups. Agency software already covers parts of the work, and the market size is unverified.

challenge_check.killer: No full killer found. Partial rivals: nCino KYC/DocFox (client due diligence and audit trail), PropWorx (trust cashbooks and audit reports), PayProp (route to trust-account exemption, which removes the audit duty), the Moonstone FICA Toolkit, and consultants such as MJK Inc. Not reached: how many agencies hold exemptions, and whether MyPPRA prompts audit prep.
challenge_check.reason: I found no product that runs the whole workflow for a small agency: RMCP upkeep, risk register, training log, RCR, the Directive 12 RMCP upload by 31 October, and audit prep. The competition is still partial. nCino KYC (formerly DocFox) and TVA cover client due diligence and its audit trail. The Moonstone toolkit is a template kit at R4,995. Three things weaken the idea. The trust-account audit is filed by the auditor. PropWorx already produces trust audit reports. PayProp sells a route to trust-account exemption, which removes the audit duty and shrinks the audit-pack market. The FIC also discourages generic templates, so consultants and law firms are likely rivals. The duty clearly bites: there are fines, the FFC is tied to compliance, and Directive 12 starts this year.
